items.text: A silent afternoon. Enigma sits at his desk, trying to picture a field of grass.
But something else always pushes its way in—something bitter, something that tastes of rust. After several failed attempts, he pulls open the drawer and looks at what's inside.
A pistol.
A Luger P08. Practical for self-defense. A precise, purely scientific creation.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Greta Hofmann.
He says the name quietly.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Those who aren't taken by the "Storm"—where do they go when they die?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'd like to verify it for myself.
Cemetery
... Never afraid of sacrifice, she followed her own path ...
... and her fearlessness and perseverance ultimately ...
Ms. Marcus.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Oh, you've arrived.
The young investigator lowers her head. A moment later, she manages a slightly easier expression.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It's good to see you, Ms. Semmelweis.
Semmelweis glances at the papers in Marcus's hand. They're crumpled, and near where the ink has smeared, new letters have been neatly filled in.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Relax. Everything will go smoothly.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Where are the others?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The Foundation's memorial ceremony has already ended. It was solemn. Almost everyone came to express their condolences. They just all had to get back to their work.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Well, at least this cemetery will always remain open.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I was more so wondering about those colleagues you're familiar with. Ms. Kakania, for example? I thought she'd be accompanying you.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She had to go through a few more rounds of inquiries, so she couldn't make it. She did send a bouquet of flowers, though.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It was just like the one you brought: a beautifully arranged bouquet of white chrysanthemums.
Semmelweis nods and surveys the figures scattered around them.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And Enigma? Where's he gone off to? Weren't they each other's only family?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I heard he was the one who pushed for the "Hofmann Knot" name. Rather admirable, if you ask me.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But now, at that very sister's funeral, our Mr. Adler is nowhere to be found.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: A few days ago, Mr. Enigma helped me sort through Madam Hofmann's possessions.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Then he left all in a hurry.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Later, I received word from Laplace that he'd barred the door to his office.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Hah. So he's chosen escapism, then.
The conversation ends there.
He, the two of them, and all the rest gathered here are little more than acquaintances to one another.
Familiar only in their mourning.
At last, Marcus speaks again.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: There was a mailing list among Madam Hofmann's possessions.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: On the train to Vienna, she asked me a question, hoping I could "read" its answer.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "What is the best way for someone to defend themselves if they cannot use arcane skills?"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I read the answer she expected. She asked because she was preparing a gift.
The words fly out of her like fired bullets.
What a rare thing, the chance to ease unbearable grief simply by sharing it.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mr. Enigma packed the list, her documents, her ID badge, and her diary into a box. Madam Hofmann's entire life ... reduced to a tiny box.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Then he stopped. And he asked me—

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Where do you think Greta has gone?
The ink on the paper in her hand starts to run again.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Where has she gone? Heaven? Hell? Has this 'Storm' washed them away too?"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Those who aren't lost to the 'Storm'—where do they go?"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Will I see her again someday? Will all of us, any of us, see her again?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If only I'd known earlier that the gift she was preparing was a birthday present for him, then instead of taking care of me and celebrating my first day as a Foundation Investigator, she could have ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If only my arcane skill were more useful! If only I'd read what would happen on that stage!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If only the future were written out as words on a page!
Semmelweis says nothing. She only raises her hand gently.
But before that touch can reach her, Marcus draws a deep breath and forces her "what ifs" back down.
There is nowhere to turn for answers. No point in blaming herself. What's done is done.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I told him I hoped Madam Hofmann had gone somewhere with no "Storm" and started a new life, even if that means we'll never see her again.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: In the end, he said he needed to think about my answer. He hasn't left his room since.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I can understand that. I don't want to be here either. But I have to, because I want people to know that they don't need to worry about me anymore.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Escapism is a natural reaction to grief. Just because you don't want to face it doesn't mean you're heartless, don't you think?
She waits almost stubbornly for an answer.
Semmelweis glances toward the distant grave and smiles softly.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Look at you saying all that without stammering. You see? There's no need to worry.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: S-Sorry. I-I shouldn't have suddenly ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No, you're right. Everyone handles grief differently.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Let's go. I'd like to hear how your training is going. I'm sure Greta would be proud of how much her little apprentice has grown.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Alright, Ms. Semmelweis.
She nods solemnly.
They pass through the gathering crowd and stand before the grave.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: *deep breath*
She gazes at the small box in the hole. Everything suddenly feels unreal.
She desperately wishes it were unreal, just some nightmare her mind conjured under pressure.
But every book has an end.
It's time to turn the page.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann was an exemplary Foundation Investigator, a dependable teammate, and my dearest mentor.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She never cowered in the face of sacrifice. She followed ...
A hand settles on her back. Semmelweis finishes the sentence for her.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She followed her own path until the end ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... pursuing the truth with a resolute heart.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And, ultimately, it was her fearlessness and perseverance that brought us the knot that allows us to cross the "Storm."
That's why I have to cherish every chance to keep the story going.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She inspired many, none more than myself. She gave me the courage to leave the Flannan Isles, allowing me to witness and read so many new things. So standing here, I vow ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: To continue to seek what she sought, what we all seek! A world after 1999!
Because I want to see the world you believed in.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I will persevere as she did. I will keep reading, keep writing, record every experience, every feeling!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... will never forget what you've done for us. For me.
